_comment: Cocktail-table seating hints, matched by slugified clean title (the same slug derive_id builds), so ROM dump suffixes like (U) or [!] don't matter. Three seating values, and the distinction is the whole point of the feature: 'alternating' = turn-based, so the screen can flip 180 between turns and both players read it right-way-up from opposite sides — this is what real Pac-Man cocktail cabinets did. 'same-side' = simultaneous play on one shared orientation, so both players must sit on the SAME side of the table; flipping mid-game would blind one of them. 'either-side' = the playfield is radially symmetric or orientation-agnostic, so opposite seats work with no flip at all. Warlords is the classic 'either-side' game and it is an Atari arcade title, not an NES one — the NES library has essentially nothing in that category, which is why the list below is empty. Unlisted games default to same-side.
